genePlain.CYP2C19: CYP2C19 is a liver enzyme. It switches some medicines on and breaks others down.
genePlain.CYP2C9: CYP2C9 is a liver enzyme that clears several common medicines out of the body.
genePlain.VKORC1: VKORC1 is the protein warfarin blocks. Some versions are blocked more easily, so less drug is needed.
genePlain.SLCO1B1: SLCO1B1 is a transporter that pulls statins from the blood into the liver.
genePlain.DPYD: DPYD makes the enzyme that breaks down the chemotherapy drugs 5-FU and capecitabine.
genePlain.NUDT15: NUDT15 helps clear thiopurine drugs. Low activity lets the drug damage bone marrow.
genePlain.TPMT: TPMT helps clear thiopurine drugs. Low activity lets the drug damage bone marrow.
genePlain.CYP3A5: CYP3A5 is an enzyme that clears tacrolimus, a transplant anti-rejection drug.

CYP2C19 *2.effect: no-function allele: the enzyme is not made

CYP2C19 *17.label: CYP2C19*17
CYP2C19 *17.effect: increased-function allele: the enzyme works faster

VKORC1 -1639A.label: VKORC1 -1639A
VKORC1 -1639A.effect: more sensitive to warfarin, so a lower dose is needed

SLCO1B1 *5.label: SLCO1B1*5
SLCO1B1 *5.effect: reduced liver uptake of statins, so more stays in the blood

DPYD *2A.label: DPYD*2A

CYP3A5 *3.label: CYP3A5*3
CYP3A5 *3.effect: no-function allele, and the common version worldwide

Ultrarapid Metabolizer.implication: Increased clopidogrel active metabolite formation; lower on-treatment platelet reactivity; no association with higher bleeding risk
Ultrarapid Metabolizer.recommendation: If considering clopidogrel, use at standard dose (75 mg/day)

Rapid Metabolizer.implication: Normal or increased clopidogrel active metabolite formation; normal or lower on-treatment platelet reactivity; no association with higher bleeding risk
Rapid Metabolizer.recommendation: If considering clopidogrel, use at standard dose (75 mg/day)

Normal Metabolizer.implication: Normal clopidogrel active metabolite formation; normal on-treatment platelet reactivity
Normal Metabolizer.recommendation: If considering clopidogrel, use at standard dose (75 mg/day)

Likely Intermediate Metabolizer.implication: Reduced clopidogrel active metabolite formation; increased on-treatment platelet reactivity; increased risk for adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events
Likely Intermediate Metabolizer.recommendation: Avoid standard dose clopidogrel (75 mg) if possible. Use prasugrel or ticagrelor at standard dose if no contraindication.

Intermediate Metabolizer.implication: Reduced clopidogrel active metabolite formation; increased on-treatment platelet reactivity; increased risk for adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events
Intermediate Metabolizer.recommendation: Avoid standard dose (75 mg) clopidogrel if possible. Use prasugrel or ticagrelor at standard dose if no contraindication.

Likely Poor Metabolizer.implication: Significantly reduced clopidogrel active metabolite formation; increased on-treatment platelet reactivity; increased risk for adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events
Likely Poor Metabolizer.recommendation: Avoid clopidogrel if possible. Use prasugrel or ticagrelor at standard dose if no contraindication.

Poor Metabolizer.implication: Significantly reduced clopidogrel active metabolite formation; increased on-treatment platelet reactivity; increased risk for adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events
Poor Metabolizer.recommendation: Avoid clopidogrel if possible. Use prasugrel or ticagrelor at standard dose if no contraindication.

Ultrarapid Metabolizer.implication: Increased metabolism of citalopram and escitalopram to less active compounds when compared to CYP2C19 rapid and normal metabolizers. Lower plasma concentrations decrease the probability of clinical benefit.
Ultrarapid Metabolizer.recommendation: Consider a clinically appropriate alternative antidepressant not predominantly metabolized by CYP2C19. If citalopram or escitalopram are clinically appropriate, and adequate efficacy is not achieved at standard maintenance dosing, consider titrating to a higher maintenance dose.

Rapid Metabolizer.implication: Increase in metabolism of citalopram and escitalopram to less active compounds when compared to CYP2C19 normal metabolizers. Lower plasma concentrations decrease the probability of clinical benefit.
Rapid Metabolizer.recommendation: Initiate therapy with recommended starting dose. If patient does not adequately respond to recommended maintenance dosing, consider titrating to a higher maintenance dose or switching to a clinically appropriate alternative antidepressant not predominantly metabolized by CYP2C19.

Normal Metabolizer.recommendation: Initiate therapy with recommended starting dose

Likely Intermediate Metabolizer.implication: Reduced metabolism when compared to CYP2C19 normal metabolizers. Higher plasma concentrations may increase the probability of side effects.
Likely Intermediate Metabolizer.recommendation: Initiate therapy with recommended starting dose. Consider a slower titration schedule and lower maintenance dose than normal metabolizers.

Intermediate Metabolizer.implication: Reduced metabolism when compared to CYP2C19 normal metabolizers. Higher plasma concentrations may increase the probability of side effects.
Intermediate Metabolizer.recommendation: Initiate therapy with recommended starting dose. Consider a slower titration schedule and lower maintenance dose than normal metabolizers.

Likely Poor Metabolizer.implication: Reduced metabolism of citalopram and escitalopram to less active compounds when compared to CYP2C19 normal and intermediate metabolizers. Higher plasma concentrations may increase the probability of side effects.
Likely Poor Metabolizer.recommendation: Consider a clinically appropriate antidepressant not predominantly metabolized by CYP2C19. If citalopram or escitalopram are clinically appropriate, consider a lower starting dose, slower titration schedule and 50% reduction of the standard maintenance dose as compared to normal metabolizers.

Poor Metabolizer.implication: Reduced metabolism of citalopram and escitalopram to less active compounds when compared to CYP2C19 normal and intermediate metabolizers. Higher plasma concentrations may increase the probability of side effects.
Poor Metabolizer.recommendation: Consider a clinically appropriate antidepressant not predominantly metabolized by CYP2C19. If citalopram or escitalopram are clinically appropriate, consider a lower starting dose, slower titration schedule and 50% reduction of the standard maintenance dose as compared to normal metabolizers.

Normal Metabolizer.implication: TPMT NMs have lower erythrocyte concentrations of TGN metabolites and higher concentrations of MeMPNs compared to TPMT IMs and TPMT PMs. This is the 'normal' pattern.
Normal Metabolizer.recommendation: Initiate therapy with standard starting dose (e.g., 2 mg/kg/day for autoimmune diseases). During therapy, adjust doses of azathioprine based on disease-specific guidelines. It usually takes at least 2 weeks to reach steady state after each dose adjustment.

Intermediate Metabolizer.implication: TPMT IMs have moderate to high erythrocyte concentrations of TGN metabolites and low concentrations of MeMPNs compared to TPMT NMs.
Intermediate Metabolizer.recommendation: Initiate therapy with reduced starting doses (30-80% of standard starting dose) if standard starting dose is ≥2 mg/kg/day. If starting dose is already below standard starting dose, dose reduction might not be necessary. During therapy, adjust the doses of azathioprine based on the degree of myelosuppression and disease-specific guidelines. It usually takes at least 2-4 weeks of stable dosing to reach steady state after each dose adjustment.

Normal Metabolizer.implication: Lower dose-adjusted trough concentrations of tacrolimus and decreased chance of achieving target tacrolimus concentrations.
